long_biography.plain_text:
Vassilis Constantakopoulos grew up in a farming family in Diavolitsi and moved to Athens during Greece's civil war. He attended night school while working, then accepted an unpaid berth at eighteen. Twenty years at sea took him from deck boy to master and supplied the experience and savings for his first shipowning ventures. In 1974 he founded Costamare, later committing the fleet to container shipping when the sector was still new to Greek owners.

Shipping financed a second ambition in his native Messinia. Constantakopoulos spent decades assembling land for a high-end destination designed to keep jobs in the region. He founded TEMES in the late 1990s, and Costa Navarino's first resort area opened in 2010. He also founded an industrial-minerals business and backed marine environmental education, but Costamare remained the original wealth engine. Before retiring, he transferred management and administration of his companies to his three sons.
